title: Operator Toolkit: taskified runbooks + interactive admin utility
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Background: Our support team spends a lot of time following multi-step runbooks for common incidents (model OOMs, KV cache corruption, emergency model switchovers). Runbooks are maintained in Confluence and as ad-hoc shell scripts in GitHub. This ticket aims to create a unified Operator Toolkit that: 1) surfaces runbooks as taskable steps in the support portal (runbooks-as-tasks), 2) provides an interactive admin CLI (local + CloudShell) for safe execution of those steps with typed verification and audit logging, and 3) wires basic automation for low-risk steps (restart router, clear prefix cache) to reduce MTTR.

Goals and success metrics:
- Convert top 8 incident runbooks to taskified workflows with explicit prechecks and postchecks.
- Provide admin-cli v1 with dry-run, step-confirmation, idempotency checks, and automatic audit events to the console logs.
- Reduce average time-to-resolution for repeatable incidents by 30% in the pilot squad within 6 weeks.
- Ensure all task executions produce linked tickets/records in Support tooling and are replayable for post-mortem.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- We will not implement full playbook orchestration (eg. dynamic branching) in v1; tasks are linear with optional checks. This keeps scope small and review surface low.
- Admin CLI will require explicit feature flags for destructive operations. Default mode is safe/dry-run.
- We debated a web-based executor vs CLI-first. Chose CLI-first because many SREs prefer terminal workflows and it is easier to integrate with CloudShell and private deployments.
- For audit logs we integrate with existing Console event stream (console-events Redwood internal endpoint) rather than creating a separate store.

Implementation plan:
1) Schema for taskified runbooks (YAML) and parser in tooling repo.
2) Small Confluence importer to seed YAML runbooks from existing canonical pages.
3) Admin CLI MVP (Python/Go) with commands: toolkit runbook list | show | execute --step N --dry-run | rollback.
4) Support portal integration: list active runbooks, attach a runbook-task to an incident, show live step status (via websocket to a lightweight backend).
5) Automation agents: implement guarded automation for low-risk steps behind feature flags; each automated step must include pre-check and rollback plan.

Acceptance criteria:
- 8 runbooks migrated and runnable via CLI in dry-run.
- Audit events created in Console for each executed step.
- Security sign-off for CLI auth model (token exchange + short-lived session tickets).
- Demo and runbook walkthrough with Support, SRE, and PM.

Links / artifacts:
- Confluence seed pages: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/Runbook+Index
- Prototype CLI repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/operator-toolkit (WIP branch: eng/ENG-9187)
- Design notes: https://docs.redwood/ops/operator-toolkit-spec (internal)
- Example runbook YAML template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/operator-toolkit/blob/eng/ENG-9187/docs/runbook-template.yaml
